words.gloss: adhering to the side of justice

ai.literal: Impartiality called one thing is indeed good, if, towards all classes of people, adhering to the side of justice, to conduct oneself is achieved.
ai.translation: The single virtue called impartiality is indeed excellent, if one can conduct oneself with equal fairness towards all classes of people.
ai.modern: நண்பர், பகைவர், அயலார் ஆகிய அனைத்துப் பிரிவினரிடமும் நடுவுநிலைமையோடு நடந்து கொள்ளப் பெற்றால், தகுதி என்று சொல்லப்படும் அந்த ஒரு பண்பு மட்டுமே ஒருவருக்குப் பெரும் நன்மையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet introduces the chapter on impartiality by defining its supreme value. The word 'தகுதி' (fitness/equity) is used here to mean impartiality or fairness. The poet states that this single quality is a great virtue, provided one can practice it consistently across different 'பகுதி' (divisions or categories of people, such as friends, enemies, and strangers). The phrase 'பாற்பட்டு ஒழுகப் பெறின்' emphasizes that true impartiality lies in actively adhering to the side of justice in all one's actions.

ai.literal: The wealth of him who possesses impartiality, without decay, to his posterity protection it has.
ai.translation: The wealth of a person of upright impartiality will not diminish; it will stand as a protective shield for their posterity.
ai.modern: நடுவுநிலைமை உடையவனுடைய செல்வமானது அழிவில்லாமல் அவனுடைய சந்ததிக்குப் பாதுகாப்பாக விளங்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the enduring value of impartiality, referred to here as 'ceppam'. The author asserts that the wealth accumulated by an upright, fair-minded person does not perish or decay. Instead, it remains secure and serves as a source of strength and protection for their descendants or posterity, termed 'eccam'. The word 'eccam' literally means 'that which is left behind', referring to one's children and future generations. Thus, practicing fairness not only benefits the individual during their lifetime but also secures the well-being of their lineage.

ai.literal: Even if it yields goodness, wealth acquired by transgressing impartiality, at that very moment, to be abandoned, must let go.
ai.translation: Even if it yields great benefit, wealth acquired by departing from impartiality must be abandoned at that very moment.
ai.modern: நன்மையையே தந்தாலும், நடுவுநிலைமையைக் கடந்து பெறுகின்ற செல்வத்தை, அப்பொழுதே கைவிட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute value of integrity and impartiality over material gain. The poet argues that even if a dishonest or biased act promises to bring immense wealth or benefit ('நன்றே தரினும்'), such wealth ('ஆக்கத்தை') acquired by deviating from fairness ('நடுவு இகந்து ஆம்') must be rejected immediately ('அன்றே ஒழிய விடல்'). The phrase 'அன்றே' (that very day or moment) highlights that there should be no hesitation or delay in discarding ill-gotten gains. True virtue lies in recognizing that wealth obtained through unfair means is inherently harmful and unworthy of possession.

ai.literal: Those who are righteous and those who are not, that fact, by their respective legacy, will be seen.
ai.translation: Whether a person was righteous or unrighteous will be known by the legacy they leave behind.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் நடுவுநிலைமை உடையவரா அல்லது நடுவுநிலைமை இல்லாதவரா என்பது அவருக்குப் பின் எஞ்சியிருக்கும் புகழாலும் பழியாலும் அறியப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to identify a person of true equity and justice. The terms 'takkār' and 'takavilar' refer to those who possess equity and those who lack it, respectively. The poet asserts that their true nature is revealed through their 'eccam', which means that which is left behind, such as their reputation, deeds, or offspring. By observing what remains after them, the world can clearly perceive their true character.

ai.literal: Ruin and prosperity are not non-existent; unswervingness of the mind is the ornament to the noble.
ai.translation: Loss and gain are inevitable in life; maintaining an unswerving, impartial mind through both is the true ornament of the noble.
ai.modern: கேடும் பெருக்கமும் வாழ்வில் இல்லாதவை அல்ல; நெஞ்சத்தில் கோணாமல் நடுவுநிலையோடு இருப்பதே சான்றோர்க்கு அழகாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that adversity and prosperity are natural, inevitable phases of human life. Since these fluctuations are bound to happen, the truly noble person does not let their mind bend or deviate from fairness because of them. Keeping the mind upright and impartial in both good times and bad is the finest ornament a virtuous person can wear. The word 'kōṭāmai' (not bending) beautifully captures the essence of neutrality and justice under all circumstances.

ai.literal: "I will be ruined," let one's own mind know, if, deviating from neutrality, one does things that are not right.
ai.translation: Let a person's own mind realize, "I will be ruined," the moment they deviate from neutrality and commit unjust deeds.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் நடுவுநிலைமையிலிருந்து விலகி, அறமல்லாத செயல்களைச் செய்ய நினைத்தால், 'நான் அழியப் போகிறேன்' என்பதை அவனுடைய நெஞ்சமே அறிந்து கொள்ளட்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the self-destructive nature of losing one's impartiality. The poet states that if a person deviates from neutrality (நடுவு ஒரீஇ) and performs unjust actions (அல்ல செயின்), their own conscience or mind (தன் நெஞ்சம்) should immediately recognize (அறிக) that ruin is imminent ("கெடுவல் யான்"). The key word 'ஒரீஇ' means abandoning or deviating from, and 'அல்ல' refers to deeds that are not righteous or fair. Thus, the inner conscience acts as an early warning system, foreseeing the inevitable downfall that follows unfairness.

ai.literal: As a ruin will not consider the world, being impartial in virtue he who abided, his decline.
ai.translation: The world will not regard as a ruin or downfall the material decline of one who stands firm in impartiality and virtue.
ai.modern: நடுவுநிலையோடு அறவழியில் நிலைத்து நிற்பவனுடைய வறுமையை, உலகம் ஒரு தாழ்வாகக் கருதாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights how society values moral integrity over material wealth. When a person chooses to remain strictly impartial and righteous, they might face financial decline or poverty. However, the wise people of the world do not look down upon this loss as a true failure or ruin. Instead, such a decline is respected as a badge of honor, because the individual did not compromise their values for personal gain.

ai.literal: Like a balance rod that, having made itself level, weighs the weight, remaining without bending to one side is the ornament of the noble.
ai.translation: To remain unbiased without leaning to any one side, just like a balance scale that first levels itself and then weighs justly, is the true ornament of the wise.
ai.modern: முதலில் தன்னைச் சமமாக ஆக்கிக்கொண்டு, பின் பொருள்களின் எடையை அளவிடும் தராசுக்கோல் போல, நடுவுநிலைமையோடு அமைந்து ஒரு பக்கமும் சாயாமல் இருப்பதே சான்றோர்களுக்கு அழகாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the beautiful metaphor of a balance scale to define the virtue of impartiality. A scale must first be perfectly level before it can accurately weigh objects. Similarly, a noble person must first establish an unbiased mind and then judge matters without leaning to any one side. This steadfast fairness, free from prejudice, is described as their finest ornament.

ai.literal: Crookedness of speech that which is without is rectitude assuredly, crookedness of the mind absence if obtained.
ai.translation: If one achieves complete freedom from bias in the mind, then the absence of bias in speech is assuredly true rectitude.
ai.modern: மனதில் கோணல் இல்லாத தன்மையை ஒருவன் பெற்றால், அவனது சொல்லில் கோணல் இல்லாமல் இருப்பதுவே உறுதியாக நடுவுநிலைமை ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the relationship between inner thoughts and outer speech in practicing impartiality. The poet uses the word 'kōṭṭam' (crookedness or slant) to represent bias or favoritism. True rectitude ('ceppam') is not just speaking neutrally; it is assuredly ('orutalaiyā') achieved only when there is a complete absence of bias in the mind ('uṭkōṭṭam iṉmai'). When the mind is perfectly straight, the words ('coṟkōṭṭam illatu') will naturally reflect that true impartiality.

ai.literal: Trade to those who do trade [is true] trade, protecting others' [goods] also like their own, if they do [it].
ai.translation: For merchants, true trade consists in protecting the goods of others as they would protect their own.
ai.modern: வியாபாரம் செய்பவர்களுக்கு முறையான வியாபாரம் என்பது, பிறருடைய பொருட்களையும் தங்களுடைய பொருட்களைப் போலப் பாதுகாத்து வியாபாரம் செய்தால் அமையும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines fairness and integrity in commerce, which is a key aspect of neutrality (நடுவுநிலைமை). It states that true merchants must treat the goods and interests of their customers and others with the same care and honesty they show to their own. By protecting others' property as if it were their own, merchants establish trust and maintain ethical standards. The word 'பேணி' (protecting) highlights the active care required in business dealings, and 'தமபோல்' (like their own) sets the standard of empathy and fairness.
